items.note: S2.1.1 says a fixed linear network exchanges two banks with signs and restores every auxiliary value, matching lines 120-122. It gives none of h=100, the triple-indexed banks, the eight-row schedule or the map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a).

It has an invertible frame at each gate, intermediate frames cancelling and a route applying only an endpoint operator, which matches lines 141-148. It omits the edge operator D_vD_u^{-1}, the reason (a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate) and the formula D_out S D_in^{-1}.

It names nested subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from triple intersections. It has no nondegenerate tensor labels, no statement that the only decreasing edges are the central wires (loss h), and none of L=Ich, Wm-2N+2L or L/N=100/539 and 101/539.

It only says the endpoint operator is 'such as an address shear' and that s<Wm. There are no projections P_U or -P_{U_a}, no endpoint identity M_sink-M_source=I_m, no shear H<-H+D, and no s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.

The only allusion is S2's method, 'obtain both procedures from fixed linear networks with a strict rank saving'. There are no phase frames C_U, translation kernels aI+bX_v, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c, or C^{\otimes m} on every role. This is borderline absent.

s<Wm and s/W<m are stated as the source of the power saving, as at lines 167-175. It is not separated into bit and complex networks, does not say why the saving holds (L<N/2), and gives neither the deficits eta nor tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} with s/W<m^tau.
Cyclic distribution of rows among W roles (S2.1.1) and 'in tape order' (S2.1.5) allude to the stream lemmas. Neither the O(V) bounds nor the controlled shifts y<-y+a(controls) mod q^b are stated.

A=E_1 Pi E_2 with a partial permutation of a ones, so a rank-a shear needs a interchanges: correct in substance. It drops 'invertible' for E_1,E_2, the fixed prime q and Z/q^b, and the O(V) further work. It is an infer step with no elimination argument and no one-interchange trick (lines 1436-1443).

S2.1.6 states O(Ve^tau) for chunks of e=m^k digits but drops the row field divisible by W^k. The subtree follows the paper's route: rows split into W role streams, frames, edges by smaller interchanges, s calls on V/W, factor s/W. It misses the endpoint identity giving H<-H+D on every row, the three-update shear-to-interchange step (1535-1541), the explicit recurrence with its geometric sum, and the fixed-tape schedule.

S2.1 states O(Vu^tau), fixed tau<1, for two disjoint contiguous u-bit fields of a Cartesian-product array, as in lem:chunk-swap. The reduction from power widths (high digits as row field, padding to [q^e], base-m pieces) is not given; the subtree derives only the power-width case.

The only allusion is 'and recurse' in S2's method, together with S2.2's reliance on frames and recursive-saving. There is no change of basis P_M, no coordinate kernels C_{e_j}, no s_c child calls of C^{\otimes f}, and no H_0=bSCS.

No step concerns packed XORs at positions rho+iK, the eight whole-chunk shifts, the bad set, or its repair. The intro's whole-chunk moves with exceptional-address correction (176-179) are not carried into the plan.

The generic 's calls at parameter f on volume V/W' sits under the interchange (S2.1.4). S2.2 only relies on recursive-saving. There is no F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), no leaf cost, no row index q_0, and no condition on lambda'.

H_0 at the same bit of each of at most d chunks, cost O(Vd^{lambda'}) and error <sqrt2 2^{-p} all match lines 2651-2670. Missing are the chunk width K=floor(d^c), the parameter ranges, and exact Gaussian-dyadic evaluation with C_0 d^{C_1} guard bits before a single truncation.

F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I from character cancellation is stated correctly. The layout lemma appears only in words: 'at the stated cost' with no cost formula, no error sqrt2 l 2^{-p}, no bit-reversal B and no exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}. It also says 'd-axis' where the transform runs over the d-1 axes t_1..t_{d-1}.

Signed packing with the established O(n log n) multiplier in O(rp log(rp)) is correct. It omits B_0=2^{4p} and the centred residues, and it says the products are 'computed exactly', whereas the lemma computes exact numerators and returns Q_p(fg/r).

S3 and its sub-steps follow the paper's route: inversion F^+F^-, two forward transforms kept in a common order through the pointwise products, signed packing, then the opposite transform. Missing are the normalization (f*g)/(rM), the convolution identity F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g) with the final scale by M, P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v), and the error and cost bounds.

S4.1 says prime-length transforms go through power-of-two tensor transforms by contractions, with the permutations retained. It has no identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, no scale, no condition theta>p/alpha^4 and no costs. This is borderline stated; I took the conservative verdict.

S4.2 names Bluestein's identity turning QF_t into a cyclic convolution, but gives no chirp a_j and no formula. The second half, cancellation of the retained source permutation R giving (u*v)/S^2, appears in no step.

Only kappa=2^{-182}, 'the fixed rational parameters', 'p bits' and 'd axes of length about r' appear. There are no values of tau, lambda, c, lambda', epsilon, delta, nothing of b=ceil(log n) and p=6b, and no prime source lengths.

S5 names a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution onto distinct prime cyclic axes. It gives neither Phi: x -> prod x_i^{mu_i} with mu_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i nor the triangular digit formula quoted at line 4226.

S6 states qualitatively that the twist turns the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial mod y^r+1, with the wrap recovered on untwisting. It has no zeta=e^{pi i/r}, no map x_d -> zeta y, and no identity M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T.

S7 lists the algorithm's stages: digits, address map, three transforms, exact scalings, rounding, carries. It omits the pointwise product step, the scales S and 2^{2b+4}S, the digit scaling 2^{-b-2}, and the whole source-transform construction (A, chirp, B_0, 2^gamma, conjugation for F^+).

Error strictly below 1/2, so that rounding and carries give the exact product, is correct (4723-4733). It gives no error chain (E_s, E_w), no bound 448b 2^{-b+gamma}<=448b 2^{-3b/4}, and no use of gamma<=b/4 or p=6b.

'Every cost-table term at most p^{1-2kappa}, total O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa})' matches 4982-4994. Missing are V=Tp=Theta(n), the seven powers and their margins with min g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, and the absorption of log p factors into p^kappa that turns 1-2kappa into 1-kappa.
S0 lists nlogn-conjecture among its dependencies and states the bound, but no step says the bound refutes an eventual c_A n lg n lower bound or gives liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0.

errors.says: Prime-length Fourier transforms reduce to power-of-two d-axis transforms of precision p followed by a normalized cyclic convolution.
errors.paper: Resampling gives RF_s=2^gamma B_0 QF_t A, so the power-of-two transform sits between two contractions. The middle factor QF_t is itself evaluated as a chirp cyclic convolution, not followed by one (3812-3813, 3921-3923, 194-195).

errors.says: Two disjoint contiguous address chunks of e=m^k digits can be interchanged in O(Ve^tau) time.
errors.paper: The proposition requires radix-q digits and a row field preceding both chunks whose length is divisible by W^k (1482-1484). The plan drops this hypothesis, which arbitrary widths need lem:chunk-swap to supply.

errors.says: Parallel butterfly layers and address interchanges compute a d-axis synthetic transform.
errors.paper: The synthetic transform runs over the d-1 axes t_1..t_{d-1} of polynomial records; the last axis is the coefficient index (2953-2955, 4343).

errors.says: Polynomial products in the ring are computed exactly by signed packing in O(rp log(rp)).
errors.paper: The lemma computes the exact Gaussian-integer numerators of fg, then returns the truncated normalized product Q_p(fg/r), with error <sqrt2 2^{-p} (3228-3231).

chain: The plan follows the paper's top-level route in order: two rank-saving tape procedures, synthetic transforms over C[y]/(y^r+1) with packed products, Gaussian resampling and chirp, the CRT map, the phase twist, exact recovery, the cost table. The interchange branch has the right skeleton (network, frames, nested subspaces, s<Wm, s calls on V/W, triangular factorization) but none of its quantitative core (Wm-2N+2L, L/N=100/539, the endpoint identity, tau=1-2^{-50}). The butterfly-layer branch thins to the single asserted step S2.2, with no complex phase interface, phase-frame recursion, packed selected-bit addition or layer recurrence. Downstream, the source-permutation cancellation is missing and S9 asserts the final bound without the margins or Tp=Theta(n).

steps.note: There is a fixed linear network that exchanges two banks with signs and restores auxiliary values. There is no h=100, no triple indexing, no N or m=h^3, and no map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a).

The plan says intermediate frames cancel, leaving an endpoint operator. The mechanism (a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}) is missing, as is the fact that each edge costs only a change of frame.

Nested subspaces of an m-dimensional space are attached to the gates. It does not say they are nondegenerate subspaces of F^{\otimes3}, or that the only decreasing edges are the central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h.
S2.1.3 only implies that the nested subspaces determine the number of smaller calls. It has no rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U and no N rank-one source edges. The allusion is thin; it is close to absent.
No step gives sum|Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich, or s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
s<Wm is stated as the decisive property, but not why it holds: no L/N=100/539 or 101/539 below 1/2, and no deficit N-2L>0.
It says only that the endpoint operator is 'such as an address shear'. It has no identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m and does not say the shear H<-H+D falls on every role.

A rank-a matrix factors as E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones, so a shear needs a interchanges (S2.1.5). Each edge becomes smaller interchanges (S2.1 method), and a node makes s calls (S2.1.4). Invertibility of E_i and the O(V) extra work are omitted.
The recursion appears in words (s calls on volume V/W, factor s/W<m), giving tau<1. There is no explicit F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), no s/W<m^tau, and no tau=1-2^{-50} from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20.

central.summary: Only C8 is reconstructed. The plan names the central chain in the paper's order (network, frames, nested subspaces, s<Wm, triangular factorization, recursion with factor s/W<m) but carries almost none of its content. Missing are h, N and m, the single decreasing central edge, rank equals dimension change, the budget Wm-2N+2L, L/N<1/2, the endpoint identity and tau=1-2^{-50}. A reader learns that s<Wm drives the power saving but not why it holds.
